name: Bogner
why: Munich ski house from 1932 — Maria Bogner’s stretch pant, the quilted ski jacket, FIRE+ICE — with one Madison Avenue store; majority-owned by Katjes since 2025.
origin: Founded in 1932 in Munich, Germany by Willy Bogner Sr. (Maria Bogner presented the first collection in 1948).

craft_evidence.owned: none stated: no owned factory, mill or workshop on bogner.com; shoes made since 2010 by an unnamed family-run business in Marche, Italy (shoe page)
craft_evidence.makers: clothing PDPs: none (0/197); one shoe maker named in news: Cappelletti S.r.L. (CTP25 sneaker)
craft_evidence.mills: Balli weaving mill (Italy) named on 2/197 PDPs (Kendo vest, Milan jacket); otherwise generic "Italian" fabric on 3 more
craft_evidence.madein: clothing: garment country on 0/197 PDPs (fabric origin Italy on 5); shoes: Made in Italy stated for the shoe collection
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: 1932 Willy Bogner Sr. founds the Willy Bogner Ski company (import of skis, equipment, Norwegian knitwear), Munich HQ; 1948 Maria Bogner stretch stirrup pants; 1955 B-zipper
craft_evidence.process: shoes only (about 50 pieces per pair, handmade in Marche); no clothing process documented
craft_evidence.reasoning: Bogner owns no making that its site shows and names no garment makers; garment country of origin appears on none of 197 men clothing pages, and only two name a mill (Balli). The heritage is dated and placed (1932, 1948 stretch pants, 1955 B-zipper), and the shoes are documented as made in Italy by an unnamed Marche family business, which lifts it above a 1 but not to a 3.
